biosphereworlds.configuration.solar_guar: Generate up to three small orbital pedestals with ghast, phantom and blaze spawners. Active within 96 blocks of a player; one mob per cycle, 30–60 seconds between cycles. Nearby system limits: 2 ghasts, 3 phantoms, 3 blazes. Phantoms only at night. No guardians in Peaceful or with mob spawning disabled. Cages can be destroyed and are not rebuilt. New Solar worlds only.
biosphereworlds.configuration.SolarOrbit: Solar-only planets, distances, numeric temperature and guardian cages. General sphere values are independent in SolarSystems.toml. Automatic bridges, classic grid spacing and hemispheres are disabled. The sun has no moons. Applies to new worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.solar_plan: Exact number of orbital planets, excluding the central Stronghold sphere and mineral satellites. They occupy up to three orbital bands around the center. Applies only to new Solar worlds; saved worlds retain their settings.

Minimum empty gap between sphere surfaces, in blocks, never center-to-center distance. Also separates the central sphere from the inner orbit. Orbital geometry can produce larger gaps. Applies only to new Solar worlds; saved worlds retain their settings.
biosphereworlds.configuration.solar_syst: Minimum empty gap between the outer envelopes of neighboring systems, in blocks. System size is calculated from planet sizes and distances automatically. Applies only to new Solar worlds; saved worlds retain their settings.
biosphereworlds.configuration.solar_clim: Integer slider: 0 = magma/lava center, warm inner planets and cold exterior. 1 = packed-ice center, cold inner planets and warm exterior. The middle stays temperate. Applies only to new Solar worlds; saved worlds retain their settings.
biosphereworlds.configuration.title: Biosphere Worlds Configuration
biosphereworlds.configuration.Settings.t: Sphere size and spacing, shell and bridge blocks, structures, edge ocean and satellites.
biosphereworlds.configuration.radius.too: Maximum sphere radius in blocks (128 by default). Applies to new worlds. Solar uses this value without a separate radius cap; enable close_open_top to close spheres cut by world height. The central Stronghold has a fixed size.
biosphereworlds.configuration.min_radius: Minimum sphere radius. Set equal to the maximum for fixed sizes or lower for random sizes. Must be positive and no greater than the maximum in Solar. Applies to new worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.spacing.to: Distance between sphere center points on the grid, in blocks. Only affects newly generated worlds. Disabled in Solar Systems; use planet and system distances instead.
biosphereworlds.configuration.center_y.t: Sphere center Y for new worlds. Solar planets use this exact value; the central Stronghold stays at Y=127. World height clips oversized spheres.
biosphereworlds.configuration.sphere_blo: Block ids used for the sphere shells; each sphere picks one deterministically from its grid position. On this screen you can edit, reorder or remove the existing entries, but new entries must be added to the config file by hand. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.only_upper: Generate only the upper half of each sphere. Only affects newly generated worlds. Disabled in Solar Systems, which uses complete spheres.
biosphereworlds.configuration.close_open: Close spheres cut by build height with a flat shell cap at the top buildable Y. Also applies to new Solar worlds. Disabled means no flat cap; sphere radius is preserved in both cases.
biosphereworlds.configuration.bedrock_mo: Bedrock at the world floor. floor: keep the bedrock_floor surface rule at the bottom of the world. none: no bedrock at the bottom, the floor is deepslate instead (the Create Diesel Generators pumpjack needs bedrock, so it will not work with this value). shell: floor plus a 3-block bedrock lining on the inside of the glass shell in the lower half of each sphere; with only_upper_hemisphere enabled it behaves exactly like floor. Only affects newly generated chunks.
biosphereworlds.configuration.generate_b: Generate bridges between adjacent spheres. Only affects newly generated worlds. Always disabled in Solar Systems.
biosphereworlds.configuration.bridge_blo: Block id used for the bridges (for example minecraft:oak_planks). Only affects newly generated worlds. Unused in Solar Systems: automatic bridges are disabled.
biosphereworlds.configuration.bridge_rad: Radial thickness of the bridge tube; larger values make thicker bridges. Only affects newly generated worlds. Unused in Solar Systems: automatic bridges are disabled.
biosphereworlds.configuration.restrict_s: Keep structure starts inside the spheres instead of letting them generate in the void. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.structure_: Extra inward margin, in blocks, between a structure start and the sphere edge. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.debug_biom: Log outside-sphere biome lookup routes at DEBUG level. Diagnostic only: it does not change world generation.
biosphereworlds.configuration.edge_ocean: Flood the band next to the sphere shell with ocean: the terrain is clamped down to a flat floor so water reaches the glass. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Width of the ocean band, as a percentage of the sphere radius (0-100). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Depth of the ocean floor below sea level (63), in blocks (0-100). Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.satellites: Generate small satellite spheres above each main sphere. Satellites are always complete spheres with a glass shell and a stone body. With center_y = 62 they only fit when the main radius is below roughly 200-300 blocks. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum number of satellites around each main sphere (0-64). 0 disables them even when satellites_enabled is true. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Minimum satellite radius, as a percentage of the main sphere radius (1-100, default 8). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum satellite radius, as a percentage of the main sphere radius (1-100, default 12). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Minimum gap between the satellite and main sphere surfaces, as a percentage of the main radius. The absolute minimum is satellites_min_gap_blocks. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum gap between the satellite and main sphere surfaces, as a percentage of the main radius. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Absolute minimum gap, in blocks, between the satellite and main sphere surfaces. It is also the safety margin from the cell border and from other satellites. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Minimum elevation angle of the satellites above the main sphere center, in degrees (0-90). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum elevation angle of the satellites above the main sphere center, in degrees (0-90). Only affects newly generated worlds.

Block ids or #tags that must never be chosen for a satellite core (default: ancient debris, nether quartz, nether gold and #c:ores_in_ground/deepslate). Invalid entries are ignored with a warning. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.

Block ids or #tags added to the satellite core candidates even when they are not in #c:ores_in_ground/stone. Invalid entries are ignored with a warning. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.
Selection weight for ores added by other mods; vanilla ores keep their own weights. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.

Ore blocks per 1000 core blocks for ores added by other mods (20 = 2%). Vanilla ores keep their own densities. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.
